overview: Two very different worm body plans that cause overlapping but distinct disease patterns in humans.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Flatworms (tapeworms) with a flattened, ribbon-like, segmented body made up of repeating proglottids.
aspects.valueB: Roundworms with a cylindrical, unsegmented body and a complete digestive tract.

aspects.label: Body Plan
aspects.valueA: Flat, ribbon-shaped, segmented into a scolex and a chain of proglottids.
aspects.valueB: Round in cross-section, unsegmented, tapering at both ends.

aspects.label: Digestive System
aspects.valueA: No digestive tract — nutrients are absorbed directly across the body surface (tegument).
aspects.valueB: Complete digestive tract with a mouth and anus.

aspects.label: Reproductive Anatomy
aspects.valueA: Most proglottids are hermaphroditic, each containing both male and female reproductive organs.
aspects.valueB: Generally have separate sexes (dioecious), with distinguishable male and female worms.

aspects.label: Examples
aspects.valueA: Taenia solium, Taenia saginata, Echinococcus granulosus.
aspects.valueB: Ascaris lumbricoides, Enterobius vermicularis, hookworms, Strongyloides.

aspects.label: Common Transmission Route
aspects.valueA: Ingestion of larval cysts in undercooked meat.
aspects.valueB: Varies widely: ingestion of eggs, larval skin penetration, or vector transmission depending on species.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Round, unsegmented, complete gut, separate sexes.
